beats.say: Camels do not store water in their humps. If you cut one open, which please don't, you would not find a fish tank.
The hump is fat. A big lump of fat, sometimes dozens of kilos of it.
When food runs out, the camel burns that fat for energy, and the hump actually shrinks and flops over to the side, like a sad deflated beanbag.
So where does the water go? Mostly into their blood and body tissue. Camels can lose a huge share of their body water and keep walking, when that would knock most mammals out.
And when they finally find water, they don't sip. A thirsty camel can drink over a hundred liters in about ten minutes.
Keeping fat in one lump on top also helps them stay cool. If that fat were spread all over the body like a blanket, they'd overheat in the desert.
beats.text:
FAT ON TOP =
COOL EVERYWHERE
ELSE

beats.say: So the hump isn't a canteen. It's a lunchbox.
The full episode, with nine more myths, is on the channel.
